history.summary: A Vaishnava shrine within the Ujjayanta Palace grounds, built in the 19th century by Maharaja Radha Kishore Manikya; a replica of the Puri Jagannath Temple with an octagonal base and four stories, Islamic-style exterior with Hindu interiors. Some sources alternatively claim an older 1661 origin under Maharaja Govinda Manikya — conflicting dates, treat the 19th-century dating as primary. CSV town corrected: this Jagannath Bari is at Agartala (West Tripura), NOT Sabroom — town field corrected. CSV DUPLICATE: this row duplicates CSV row 1045 (‘Jagannath Bari’, Ambassa) — both refer to the same Jagannath Bari at Agartala (Ujjayanta Palace grounds); kept as a separate file per the one-file-per-row convention.

name: Jagannath Bari
town_description: Agartala is the capital of Tripura, on the Haora river near the Bangladesh border. Built up by the Manikya kings, its landmarks include the Ujjayanta Palace (now the state museum), the Tripura Government Museum, and several royal-era temples.

travel.airport: Maharaja Bir Bikram Airport, Agartala (~12 km)
travel.road: Palace Compound, Krishna Nagar, Agartala — reachable by city bus, auto-rickshaw or cab

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Rath Yatra draws the largest crowds
visitor_information.opening_hours: 4:30 AM–1:00 PM, 4:00–9:00 PM (single directory source — verify)
